The system shall not allow external customers to access district-wide data.
External customers should only see information that is directly tied to their own permit and needed to understand their obligations.
For overlapping site details, the system should show only the permit-relevant version.
Anything that could be misread outside the regulatory context should either be clearly labeled or excluded.
External customers shall be able to view summarized trends in their permit information.
External customers shall be able to view permit-specific views of their permit information.
The system shall provide a generalized map location to external customers when it is necessary to understand their own records.
The system shall not provide external customers with the same level of granular detail used by district staff for internal analysis.
The system shall not expose combined data that could reveal other facilities to external customers.
Labels shown to external customers shall remain plain and regulatory.
The system shall restrict or omit internal-only report types for external customers.
Customer-facing terminology should be translated into plain language whenever an internal term might be confusing or too staff-specific.
If a regulatory label is important for legal accuracy, the system should keep the label and add a customer-friendly explanation next to it.
The system should not expose internal shorthand or report names that only staff would understand unless there is no clearer public equivalent.
Staff accounts shall be approved by the district.
External customer accounts shall be approved by verifying that the person is authorized for the relevant permit or company.
Account changes shall take effect only after approval.
Simple contact updates may take effect immediately if they do not affect permissions.
When a person changes roles or leaves, their access shall be adjusted or removed right away.
When a person changes roles or leaves, the person shall retain only the minimum access needed.
For external accounts, the account shall follow the current authorized contact list.
In most cases, the system shall keep the user's current access until the change is approved.
If a pending change involves reducing access because of a role change, a security concern, or separation from the district, the system shall suspend sensitive permissions immediately.
The system shall automatically revoke access in clear cases such as an employee leaving, a permit authorization expiring, or a customer losing authority to act for an account.
The system shall support access changes that take effect on the effective date of a permit transfer or an authorized contact change instead of immediately.
The system shall support scheduling removals or role changes for a specific cutoff time when needed to avoid disrupting a reporting cycle or ongoing review.
If the effective date arrives before approval is finalized, the change must not go live until approval is finalized.
If the underlying permit or contact change is reversed, any pending access change based on it must be canceled automatically.
In both of these cases, the system must leave the current access in place or revert to the last valid state rather than partially applying any change.
